Hi Oliver — great questions. I put together a short summary and attached two artifacts: a proposed MAP workbook (proposed_MAP_v1.xlsx) and our rate card excerpt (rate_card_v3.pdf). High level answers below; details in attachments.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Phased commits: discounts apply to "committed units" starting at the effective date of the milestone being met. Example below.
- Ramp windows: we recommend a 90-day evaluation window per milestone with a soft cap (no hard throttle) and explicit burst tiers — small bursts are free, larger bursts bill at "burst rate" which is higher than committed rate but lower than on-demand list.
- Overage protections: we can set a monthly soft cap and notify at 80%/95% with automatic fallback to a lower-cost model or throttle if desired.

Example (illustrative):
- Baseline list rate: $0.60 per 1K tokens (generation + context).
- Committed rate (after hitting a milestone): 30% discount -> $0.42 per 1K tokens for committed volume.
- Ramp free buffer: first 500K tokens/month for the initial milestone (first 30 days) are covered as evaluation credits.
- Burst tiers during ramp:
  * Tier 1 (ad-hoc spikes up to 2x daily baseline): billed at $0.75 per 1K tokens (discounted burst rate).
  * Tier 2 (sustained >2x baseline beyond 48 hours): billed at list rate unless you opt for a temporary burst add-on.
- Hard cap: optional — we can gate at the monthly soft cap you choose. By default, we do NOT hard throttle; we prefer fallbacks.

Next steps: if the numbers above look directionally right, I can:
1) Update the MAP workbook with your target baseline and proposed quarterly commit percentages.
2) Lock in a formal burst add-on price and duration in the SOW.

Thanks Hannah. Confirming internal ops:

- Discount bands for EA-2026-117 (approved by pricing committee at this stage):
  * Q1 commit (25% committed capacity): 10% discount applied to committed units effective the day the milestone is met.
  * Q2 commit (50%): 20% discount on new committed units effective on milestone date; prior committed portion keeps its earlier discount (no retroactive re-price).
  * Q3 commit (100%): 30% discount on incremental committed units from that milestone forward.

- Retroactivity: discounts apply only from the milestone effective date forward. We do not retroactively adjust prior billing periods. (This is consistent with our standard commit phasing policy.)

- Eval credit: We can offer a one-time 500K token credit applied against the first invoice once the MAP is signed. That credit is not billable and will be documented in the SOW as a non-recurring concession.

- Burst handling:
  * We will put the Tier 1 burst rate ($0.75/1K tokens) into the SOW for the 90-day ramp windows tied to each milestone.
  * Tier 2 sustained spikes (>48 hours above 2x baseline) will be billed at list rate unless a temporary burst add-on is purchased.
  * Soft cap/alerts: we'll set up notifications at 80%/95% of the monthly soft cap and will automatically switch to the lower-cost fallback model if you opt in. By default, no hard throttle.

Lauren — can you confirm the contract language to make sure the credit and burst tiers map cleanly to invoicing and the SOW? Oliver, let me know if you want the credit to be invoiced as a negative line item or described as a separate non-recurring concession — both are fine, we just need your preference for PO/accounting.

— Sergio
